chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the child, is his testimony allowed regarding the killing? He (peace be upon him) said: He is taken by the first of his speech, and he is not taken by the second.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a child's testimony in Islamic law if they change their statement?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the principle of 'taking the first statement' (al-awwal) for a child's testimony in homicide cases, reflecting the Shia juristic view that a child's initial utterance is less prone to fabrication or external influence. It highlights the practical application of assessing credibility based on the timing and stability of the statement rather than the child's age alone. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining evidentiary weight in the absence of adult witnesses.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Jameel who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the child, is his testimony allowed regarding the killing?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be taken by the first of his speech, and he would not be taken by the second (if he changes his statement)’.
en.sarwar: Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If children are asked to bear testimony if they did so as children it is permissible, when they grow up, to present it if they have not forgotten.’”
